summary: Submitted draft/submission.json (action=check) with draft/check-plan-config.json, draft/check-harness-config.go and the map update draft/map-v5.json carried on the candidate: a combined product for the deferred surface that recorded a client-visible configuration index the API never fills. The map adds the configuration fact (the node's latest configuration together with the log index at which it was established — written by the leader when it appends a configuration entry, adopted by followers from the log, consumed by the commitment table as the qualifying voter set, and reported by the client contract) and declares the four behavior edges that support it, each as a meaning change with a preserved explanation so nothing that depended on those behaviors loses its basis. The obligation c-reported-configuration-index states the reporting duty for that index (implementation_semantics, consumption lifecycle on fact f-latest-configuration, cited under A1 and A7 through b-config-change and b-client-apply-verify, with b-follower-append-entries and b-commit-advance as support), and is bound by bind-raft-get-configuration at the accessor declaration. The check is the surface's deterministic instance: one node is created by the package's own NewRaft and bootstraps a single-voter configuration, so the configuration entry is the only log entry and its index is the log's last index; the harness then reads the configuration future's Error, Index and Configuration, whether that configuration still contains the local voter, the value Stats publishes for the same future, and the node's state. Applicability requires the returned configuration to be the live one, and the assertion requires the reported index to equal the index at which the configuration was established, so a different number means the accessor reports an index that does not identify the configuration it returned. I verified the exact submitted harness bytes in a fresh copy of the captured module: the test passes (exit 0) and emits configuration_established with index 1 followed by configuration_index_observed with reported_index 0, stats_index "0", configuration_has_self true and log_last_index 1, reproducibly. Two mechanical issues arose and are worth recording: the map update was applied as a mechanical JSON field edit after patch matching on the previous version's long lines proved unreliable, and the trusted validator rejected the first draft because a check submission cannot carry map_path or map_changes directly — the map travelled on the candidate object instead, which is the shape the schema allows for a combined product. Counterevidence and limits are recorded: the returned Configuration value is correct and current, so callers that ignore the index are unaffected; nothing documents that the index may be unset while the same field is published as a metric; the index is available inside the main goroutine, so it is omitted rather than unavailable; and the prefix contains a single configuration entry, so a second change inside the same prefix and any downstream consumer consequence remain open. Optional preflight with the trusted validator returned valid=true; the next step would be the correspondence review of the measured comparison.
